content.rationale: The op-log read is where S3-oplog's read of the operation head, the run window and the invoking workspace meets M-layout's placement and S5-observation's (urqytyqn) observational rule; this check runs a real jj in a scratch repo and pins that a hex operation id comes back and advances after an operation, that the window between two head reads holds the entries created in between oldest first, each attributed to the workspace its work ran in, and that the invoking workspace is the one the runner stands in — that the reads leave the working copy unsettled, so a file not yet snapshotted gains no operation when the head, the window or the invoking workspace is read — and that a failed crossing carries its evidence while an absent binary is a spawn failure.
